llm.summary: The skill is coherent with a Windows file-search wrapper around Voidtools Everything, but it contains metadata/install inconsistencies and explicitly instructs the agent to perform broad agent-internal file discovery (including locating sensitive config/.env files), which raises privacy/exposure concerns the user should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name, description, SKILL.md, and the large references bundle all point to a wrapper around Voidtools Everything (ev). The declared required binary (ev) matches the purpose. However the registry/install metadata is inconsistent: SKILL.md and docs show Python/pip usage (pip install everyfile) while the install spec in metadata is labeled with kind 'node' even though it lists pip; the package record also promises binaries named ev/every/everyfile. This looks like packaging/metadata sloppiness rather than a capability mismatch, but it should be verified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to ALWAYS use this tool for any file/folder discovery — including agent-internal lookups and locating config files. The included examples show collecting .env files and exporting file lists. That scope is broad and means the agent will be guided to locate potentially sensitive data (credentials, secrets, private configuration). While this matches a file-search tool's capabilities, instructing the agent to use it for 'internal lookups' is scope creep that increases risk of exposing private files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no code files; the SKILL.md and reference docs indicate installation via pip (pip install everyfile). The registry's install entry is inconsistent (kind: 'node' but id: 'pip' and a pip-style label). There are no suspicious external download URLs or extract steps in the provided metadata. Verify the actual package source (PyPI) and package contents before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, which is proportionate. However the documentation references an optional EVERYTHING_INSTANCE env var for targeting instances and provides examples that explicitly collect .env files and other config — so while no secrets are requested, the behavior enabled by the skill makes locating secrets easy. This is a privacy concern rather than a mismatched credential request.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal model invocation settings are used. The skill does not request system-wide configuration changes or elevated persistent privileges. It relies on the Everything service running in the background (expected for this purpose).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a wrapper for Voidtools Everything and will enable extremely broad file discovery on Windows (including finding .env and other config files). Before installing: 1) Verify the package on PyPI (or the publishing source) and inspect the package contents and publisher — the registry metadata contains an install-kind mismatch that should be corrected. 2) Be aware that following the SKILL.md guidance will cause the agent to search user files and may surface sensitive data; limit autonomous use or scope searches (avoid agent-initiated system-wide scans unless you trust the environment). 3) If you need this capability, prefer installing from an official repository and audit the installed binaries (ev) to confirm they are the expected Voidtools client. 4) Consider disabling automatic/autonomous invocation for this skill in high-risk environments, and require explicit user consent before any searches that could touch secrets or whole-drive queries.
